item.title: 3 children, 1 teacher killed in Oregon school shooting, police say
item.description: Three children and a teacher were killed, and two others critically wounded, in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon. The suspect was shot and killed by a bystander.

item.title: Musk donates over $150 million to Senate GOP group, assisting Paxton
item.description: Billionaire Elon Musk is offering a nine-figure assist to Texas GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton, a decisive return to large-scale political giving for the world's richest man.

item.title: Oregon police give details on elementary school shooting
item.description: The Bend, Oregon, police chief and other officials gave an update on the elementary school shooting that killed at least three children and one teacher. The suspect was shot and killed by a bystander. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports and school safety expert Kieran Carroll has more.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz still unsafe for ships, maritime group warns
item.description: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz still face "indiscriminate attacks" even if they switch off tracking systems, a maritime risk firm warns.

item.title: High school football coach fired after calling for onside kick while leading 57-0 in 2nd quarter
item.description: An Oregon high school football coach was fired following a recent game where he called for an onside kick while his team led 57-0 in the second quarter. Mark Puleo, senior editor on the daily desk at The Athletic, joins "The Daily Report."

item.title: School safety expert discusses Oregon shooting
item.description: A bystander shot and killed the 16-year-old suspect who opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday, sources say. At least three children and one adult were killed in the shooting, multiple law enforcement sources told CBS News. Kieran Carroll, school safety expert and chief strategy officer for ZeroEyes, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Justice Dept. sues California, claims noncitizens were sent ballots
item.description: The Justice Department sued California, alleging that the federal government has identified more than 20,000 noncitizens who are unlawfully registered to vote.

item.title: Justice Department suing California for failure to provide voter info ahead of midterms
item.description: The Department of Justice is suing California after a deadline passed to provide voter records ahead of the midterm elections. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Soaring heating oil prices put struggling Maine families in a bind
item.description: The price of heating oil in Maine has soared from $3.34 per gallon one year ago to $5.97 today, a jump of roughly 79%.

item.title: Maine couple forced to choose food or heat as oil prices skyrocket
item.description: Along with diesel and gas, the price of heating oil is up, and no state depends on it more than Maine. Meg Oliver spoke with residents there, now forced to make some tough decisions.

item.title: Vance says "selling access to the White House" is "disgusting"
item.description: Vice President JD Vance told CBS News in a "Things That Matter" town hall in Michigan that anybody who is "selling access to the White House" should "suffer consequences."

item.title: New book explores sonic attacks on American diplomats known as "Havana Syndrome"
item.description: A new book, "The Havana Syndrome," investigates the alleged sonic attacks against American diplomats overseas that left many with symptoms including insomnia and memory loss. Co-authors Oriana Zill de Granados and Michael Ray share more details.

item.title: Cornell's president grilled by faculty over handling of former student's gang rape allegations
item.description: The president of Cornell University faced intense scrutiny from faculty members for his handling of allegations of gang rape that occurred at a fraternity house in 2024. Lilia Luciano reports on Wednesday's faculty senate meeting.

item.title: Michigan Senate contest earns outsized attention from Trump
item.description: Democrats hold the Michigan Senate seat on the ballot this fall, and Republican Mike Rogers is trying to pick it up for the Republicans. Ed O'Keefe has more details on the race and the latest on the Trump administration.

item.title: Massachusetts residents compete to be new voice of Boston Logan Airport: "Wicked glad you're here"
item.description: A Massachusetts competition is underway to become the new voice of Boston Logan International Airport, and the auditions are bringing out classic New England sounds. Tony Dokoupil has the wicked story.

item.title: Is Texas' Senate race a perfect storm for Democrats?
item.description: The latest Texas Senate race polls show Democrat James Talarico with a slight edge over Republican Ken Paxton. Political strategists Chuck Rocha and Erin Maguire join "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: Oregon elementary school shooter was a 16-year-old male, sources say
item.description: Law enforcement sources tell CBS News that at least three children and one adult are dead after a shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. The shooter, whom sources say was a 16-year-old male, is also dead. CBS News senior crime reporter Anna Schecter has the latest.

item.title: Vance talks economy, inflation and corruption in CBS News town hall
item.description: Vice President JD Vance sat down with "CBS Evening News" anchor Tony Dokoupil in Michigan for a "Things that Matter" town hall during his midterm campaign blitz.

item.title: Feds probing suspicious letters to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: Federal investigators said they are looking into suspicious letters containing unknown substances that were mailed to state election officials and congressional offices.

item.title: Several killed, including children, in Oregon elementary school shooting, sources say
item.description: Police say a gunman walked into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday and opened fire. Law enforcement sources said that at least four people are dead, including children. The suspect is also dead. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Vance says he would comply with Democrat-led corruption probe amid Guilfoyle's firing
item.description: Vice President JD Vance addressed public concerns with corruption within the Trump administration at a CBS News town hall Thursday, just 19 days ahead of the midterms. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Pennsylvania man who killed 8 people was "controlling" patriarch, police say
item.description: The Pennsylvania man accused of killing eight people "exercised significant control" over his family at their Erie home, police said.

item.title: 10/15: CBS Evening News
item.description: At least 4 killed in school shooting: sources; Vance addresses corruption in town hall.

item.title: Bones found in Philadelphia's "house of horrors," sources say
item.description: Bones were discovered outside the so-called "house of horrors" in Philadelphia, but it's unclear whether they are related to the ongoing investigation into Raymond "R.C." Horsch, a suspected serial killer.

item.title: Kristi Noem no longer serving as Trump envoy to Shield of the Americas
item.description: Former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration's envoy to the Shield of the Americas initiative, a State Department official said.

item.title: 10/15: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Texas' James Talarico holds razor-thin polling lead over Ken Paxton; suspect dead after shooting at elementary school in Bend, Oregon.

item.title: White House's Katie Zacharia confirms she never passed bar exam
item.description: The White House described Katie Zacharia as "uniquely qualified" to be the new press secretary.

item.title: Trump calls off plan to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution
item.description: "He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," President Trump wrote on Truth Social.

item.title: Amazon launches new AI devices that can listen and take notes
item.description: The products include a silicone wristband that can be clipped to clothing and a device that magnetically attaches to the back of a phone.

item.title: AI leaders lobby Trump health officials in government-run chat room
item.description: A Slack workspace has served as a war room for AI industry insiders and Trump administration officials to launch a rapid campaign aimed at persuading Americans to manage their healthcare and medical records on apps.
